correctness.rationale: Specified-cycle deletion is a bijection with fixed-root forests. Deleting r direct-cycle leaves and s deeper leaves leaves F(n-r-s,k) forests; their available parents number k^r(m-r-s)^s. The exact factorial-moment identity follows by the ordered-marking factor. From moments (1,0),(0,1),(1,1), the ratio E[JH]/(EJ EH) is below 1 for m>=3 because m(n-1)^2-(m-2)n^2=2n(n-m)+m>0; m=2 has E[JH]=0 and m=0,1 has H=0. First-order logarithmic expansion proves the asymptotic constant. 203 forest and 70 independent graph checks passed; finite checks are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Leaves directly attached to the unicyclic two-core versus leaves deeper in pendant trees are natural core–periphery observables. All mixed factorial moments determine their full joint distribution, and the universally strict negative conditional covariance with explicit linear-scale limit expresses structural competition not recoverable from the total-leaf marginal. The result is an exact natural finite classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
